translation:
To know or understand Parbrahm, no yogic technique of Aum nor any tantric knowledge is of any use — it is attained only when, through the Sadguru's word, the doors of the heart within are pierced open. ||25||

Baba Kabirji says: when the Sadguru's weapon-like instrument of love-imbued devotion pierces through the sense-vices lodged within a disciple, and he attains the unmani state, such a disciple no longer sets his heart on sense-pleasures and worldly enjoyment. He takes no delight in the objects of maya, because within his heart, owing to loving devotion, the restlessness, agitation and eagerness of the pain of separation are exceedingly intense. ||26||

Unmani is the state in which the soul and the mind become one, so that one is freed from maya and becomes wholly devoted to God. Yogis call it the fifth and final state — beyond waking, dream, deep sleep and turiya — the state beyond turiya, or the unmani state; in that same way the loving devotee too becomes free of maya. Thus the Sadguru's word is like the manifest form of God Himself. The definition of unmani is given in the Hathayoga Dipika:

_Shankh dundubhi nadam cha na shrunoti kadacha na, kashth vagyayate deh unmunyavasthaya dhruva ||12||_ (One does not hear even the sound of the conch or the war-drum; the body becomes like wood, firmly steadied in the unmani state.)

Meaning: [continuing the earlier passage] — When it occurred to God how, given maya's coverings, His devotees would be saved and would attain the far shore of the ocean of birth and death, God sat in peace, reflected, and commanded Sadguru Kabir: Kabir, go to this earth and, through sakhis (devotional couplets), shabdas and the like, give teaching and tell devotees about true devotion, so that some worthy souls, drowning in the ocean of existence, may be rescued from it and attain Me. ||27||

This sakhi appears in the Parcharee (hagiographic account) of Krishnadas. There, while explaining to Krishnadasji the meaning of Ramkabir, Jivanji Maharaj, speaking about Kabir, showed that this Sadguru was sent to this earth by the grace of the Guru to deliver devotees. It shows what feeling God has for His devotee. Just as, out of concern for the deliverance of devotees, Ram commanded Kabir to give teaching, in the same way one sakhi also pertains to Sadguru Jivanji Maharaj:

_Sainye shabad pukariya, tun sun re Jivandas, nij janaku parmodhake, lavo hamare pas ||50||_ (God called out and gave this command: O Jivandas, listen — teach My own worthy devotees and bring them to Me.)

In the Parcharee of Jivanji Maharaj it is said —

_Ek same Hari karuna kini, Jivandasaku agya dini, vege jao tum karo prabodhu, sab santanaki lijo sodhu._ (Once God showed grace and commanded Jivanji: go quickly, give teaching, and take care of all the sants.)

_Kabir tirath varat vakh veladi, rahe chohe jug chhahe, kabire mul nikandiya, so kon halahal khae ||28||
To kul kabiro pragata, tab vede kiya vichar, harijansu kari vinati, hamkun rahene do sansar ||29||_

(The poison-spreading creeper of pilgrimage-places and vows — which throws one into the hell of sense-desires — has spread its tendrils on every side across all four ages, casting its shade everywhere. But Sadguru Kabir has uprooted this pilgrimage-and-vow creeper entirely, root and all — that is, he made people give up pilgrimages and vows completely. So then, who would fall into the trap of this fierce poison laid down by a creeper whose very root has been destroyed? ||28|| In the community of sants who propagated devotion to Vishnu among the devotee lineage, when devotees were being caught in the trap of Vedic ritual karmakand — the trap of both the honest and the deceitful among the Vedic knowers — God, moved by concern for His devotees, manifested Sadguru Kabir on this earth. From the time Kabir began, in Kashi, to break the net of ritual karmakand, the Vedic ritualists who led people into ritual worship grew frightened and thought: our power will not prevail against these propagators of Vishnu-bhakti. So these Vedic followers pleaded and entreated the Harijans (devotees), begging: cast a little grace upon us too, so that we too may somehow get a lease of life and be allowed to remain in this world. ||29||)

When Kabirji manifested in Kashi and drove out the path of ritual karmakand, Jivanji Maharaj, as stated in the Parcharee of Krishnadas, records what Shyamdasji wrote —

_Tab kashime pragate ai, karma marag sab diyo bahai._ (When Ram commanded Kabir, he manifested in Kashi and swept away the entire path of ritual karmakand.)

In the Gyan Mahima of Shyamdasji Maharaj it is said —

_Tehi ausar Kabir pragat bhayeu, bharam karam aur sabhi gayeu._ (At that critical time when pilgrimage, vows and ritual karmakand held sway, Kabirji manifested and dispelled all the delusions of ritual religion.)

*(Kabir Ram beth vichariya: there is doubt as to whether this sakhi is truly Kabirji's own. It is an imagined story in which a dialogue takes place between Kabirji and Parbrahm Ram about how the soul can cross over — Kabirji gives the answer. Since Jivanji Maharaj is discussing this very subject here, this sakhi is quoted at this point.)

Ram, after deep reflection, said to Kabirji: O Kabir, tell the people trapped in worldly maya, with true proof, so that some genuine, worthy souls may cross this ocean of existence — and tell them how they may cross it — go into the world and explain it through the evidence of sakhis and shabdas.

Kabirji says: in the world, man wanders to many pilgrimage places, keeps vows and restraints, and wishes to live his life relying on poison — that is, on the poisonous plant of ritual karmakand — but I have utterly destroyed, root and all, this whole poisonous forest-plant of pilgrimage.

When Kabirji manifested in Kashi, the Veda (the Brahmins learned in the Veda) reflected on the path of ritual and thought that they would no longer be able to remain in Kashi. So the devotees of Shri Hari made this plea: allow us too to remain in the world. Because —

_Guru Kabir jyan vidit hai, bhakti mukti datar, jiv mulavan karane, aye jagat mojhar ||51||_ (It is known everywhere in the world that Sadguru Kabirji is the bestower of devotion and liberation; he has come into the midst of this world to grant souls liberation.)

_Riddhi siddhi hamma base, jahan mage tahan det, harijan Hari bhajo jivana, ham hi kahet he net.
Je je kar bhayo jivana, jab pragate das Kabir, karma dharma sab katke, pragat kiye Raghuvir.
Ola jhola jivana, je Sadguru diya batay, karma dharmame Raghupati, je vede dharya chhapay.
Tin lokamen tattvatha, so Sadguru diya batay, kund adavis jivana, je janke diya chhoday.
Shesh sahasra samukh je jape, so sala lakho Hanuman, so Sadguru kahyo jivana, je Gori patiko dhyan.
Kushal padi re jivana, jab Sadguru pakade hath, anek janam ramanam bin, baval dini bath ||35||_

_Chhelo janam bhayo jivana, jab Sadguru diyo updesh, sant samagamamam malyo, Ayodhya tano naresh ||36||
Asht sidh nav nidhi jivana, jahan Sadguru shabad vishvas, sol kalasu shamalo, jahan Hari ke nij das ||37||
Nabhi kamal Brahma hava, so Gokul mahi Goval, mor pichchh shir dhundhachi, so jivan vraj pratipal ||38||_

(Riddhi and siddhi — powers and treasures — dwell in us, and give wherever asked; O Harijan, worship Hari, Jivana — we ourselves only say "not that, not that." Whatever came to be, Jivana, when the servant Kabir manifested — having cut away all ritual and religion, he made Raghuvir manifest. Whatever shelter, Jivana, the Sadguru showed us, the Raghupati whom the Veda kept hidden within ritual and religion — the truth of the three worlds, that the Sadguru has shown; the twenty-eight sacred pools, Jivana, from which he freed his devotees. He who is meditated upon by the thousand-hooded Shesh with his thousand faces, whom Hanuman knows as friend — that is the one the Sadguru named, Jivana, on whom even Gauripati Shiva meditates. Good fortune has come, Jivana, now that the Sadguru has taken hold of my hand — for many births, without Ram's name, I clung to a thorny babul tree.

In this life, Jivana, since the Sadguru has given his teaching, this has become the last birth; meeting in the company of sants, I attained the king of Ayodhya. ||36||

Before the Sadguru's word, the eight siddhis and nine treasures are as nothing; the sixteen-arted dark-hued Lord is there, where Hari's own servants dwell. ||37||

He from whose lotus navel Brahma came, he himself, as the cowherd tending cows in Gokul; on whose head is the peacock-feather crown, and around whose neck shines the garland of gunja-berries — that one, Jivana, is Vraj's protector. ||38||)

In his commentary on sakhi 30, revered Yadunath Maharaj writes about the phrase "jahan mage tahan det" — to those possessed of riddhi-siddhi, it gives wherever asked. You know the story of Lakshmichand Sheth of Vrindavan. He was a man favoured by Lakshmi. To test him, someone once devised a scheme. As he was being ferried across the river in a boat, in the middle of the river the man stopped the boat and demanded of Lakshmichand: I want money right now, this very moment — give it. Lakshmichand told him to wait until they reached the other bank, but the man would not agree and pressed insistently; then, scooping handfuls of river water, the water turned into coins, and thus, in the very middle of the river, as much money as he demanded was given to him. Even though he possessed such powers, Lakshmichand set aside riddhi-siddhi and came to Vrindavan to practise loving devotion. His temple is in Vrindavan. Thus, regarding riddhi-siddhi, Vyasji says in this sakhi:

_Vyas asht siddh nav nidh, rahi thari kar jor, pamar jiv mohe lagi rahe, mai kab nirakhu Nand Kishor ||52||_ (Vyasji says the eight siddhis and nine treasures stand with folded hands before God and say: base, weak-minded people cling to us, but we, the eight riddhis and nine nidhis, only long for the day we may have the good fortune of beholding Nandkishor Krishna. Loving devotees pay no heed to riddhi; they hold only to devotion.)

Jivanji Maharaj says: the riddhi-siddhi that is in you — we have no need of it; we are capable of giving whatever anyone needs, whenever they need it. In other words, Harijans have no need at all of riddhi-siddhi, for they have already surrendered everything to Krishna. They have only to worship Shri Hari. Moreover, the Sadguru has laid out their path for them; their provision has already come about merely by their placing faith in the Sadguru's words. So riddhi-siddhi always says: let the Harijans go on worshipping Hari, we shall place no obstacle in their way.

When Kabirji manifested in Kashi and set about uprooting ritual karmakand, the Vedic paths and the Vedas pleaded that they be allowed to go on living in the world, that their existence not be destroyed, and Veda, Purana, mantra-japa, tapa, yagna and the rest began to say: we possess a certain special quality — we are capable of bestowing riddhi and siddhi, and through us people receive whatever they wish for; but even if you should choose to disregard us, do so — we for our part will place no hindrance in your way, and if, without harbouring any illusion about us, you Hari-bhaktas wish to go on worshipping Hari at your ease, do so — this is what they always say. And they say: you may go on with your Hari-bhakti, but please do not banish us from the world altogether. ||30||

With Kabirji's coming, the clouds of ritual karmakand that had gathered over the path of devotion were cleared away, and full light was granted. Rejoicing began among the devotees, and, casting aside ritual, karmakand and religion-of-works, he made Raghuvir Shri Ram manifest. ||31||

The tangles and deceptions that lay within ritual and religion — leading one down to ruin through riddhi-siddhi and the rest — the Sadguru has shown us these, showing how the Veda had kept devotion hidden under the guise of ritual and religion. Our Sadguru has revealed to us the secret of Raghupati Shri Ram, whom karma, dharma and the Vedic scriptures had kept concealed, and he has let us behold devotion to Raghupati. ||32||

The Sadguru has shown us the truth-principle that was present in the three worlds, and the name of the supreme truth, Parbrahm, by which King Janak delivered thousands of souls suffering the torments of hell — that name, "Ram," he has shown us. ||33||

The thousand-hooded Sheshnag, through his thousand mouths, continuously chants that very name of Ram; by that name Hanuman made stones float upon the sea. Such a priceless name my Sadguru has given me — the same name that Gauripati Shankar Bhagwan too continuously chants and meditates upon. ||34||

I was caught up in ritual karmakand, pilgrimage, and vows; the Sadguru helped me and, to rescue me from this suffering, showed me the path of devotion through Ram's name. After that, devotion became very easy for me. Until then, having found no one to give me Ram's name through many births, I had clung to ritual karmakand, pilgrimage and vows, painful as a thorny babul tree.

My life has become blessed, for my Sadguru took hold of me with his own hand, gave me support, and showed me the true path. So devotion became easy for me. And not just now, but through many births, without finding anyone to give me the name of Ram, which is otherwise unobtainable, I had taken refuge in ritual, religion, pilgrimage and vows, harmful as a thorny babul tree. But now that the Sadguru has given me the name of Ram, I have been saved from this painful ritual religion. ||35||

After the Sadguru gave me the teaching of Ram's name, this birth of mine has now become the very last one. I no longer have to fall into the cycle of coming and going through the womb. Now, simply through keeping company with the sants, I have attained devotion to and the presence of Ram, the king of Ayodhya.

Jivanji Maharaj says: this is my last birth. Through my Sadguru's teaching, I shall no longer have to fall into the cycle of birth and death. In the company of sants I have attained the name and the presence of Ram, the king of Ayodhya. ||36||

Before the Sadguru's word, the eight kinds of siddhi and the nine treasures are of no use at all. My place is now in the sixteen-arted Parbrahm's own abode, where the servants and devotees of Shri Hari forever dwell. ||37||

He from whose lotus navel Brahma was born — that very Parbrahm Narayan himself grazed cows in Gokul; he on whose head shines the crown of peacock feathers, and around whose neck the garland of gunja-berries — Jivanji Maharaj has recognized him, and now nothing else is needed. He is Vrajraj, the protector of Vraj. ||38||

This dialogue-satsang took place in Samvat 1983, on the thirteenth of the bright half of Aso. What was set forth in it was this: the flute-charming Lord — this Brahma is called nirgun (without attributes), but the attribute lies concealed, held in reserve, within him. Together with the five elements and the three gunas, he gathers up all the senses within himself as if into a house, folding everything away. That is to say, whatever is seen in the manifest world is but the powerful shadow of the nirgun Brahma. Everything happens by his will and wish. The soul often acts against his will; then it becomes bound by the fetter of that action, falls into the bondage of karma, and every soul must undergo the fruit of that karma. Parbrahm is nirgun — the world knows this — yet Parbrahm keeps his quality of possessing attributes (sagun) held in reserve, apart, for this manifest world, and this is the cause of the relative, dependent world, which dwells within this attribute. All beings, subtle bodies and the whole universe rest upon that very nirgun Parbrahm — that is, the world of beings remains coiled around him. Yet, despite this, no being is able to know him; all beings and subtle forms, though separated from the one supreme principle, turn away from it on account of karma — so that, even while dwelling together with him, none of them understands the dharma of Vasudev. And so they fall into birth and death and the six schools of philosophy, and waste their human birth in vain; and some fall into hollow hypocrisy and undergo the eighty-four lakh species. To this, Baba Kabirji stands witness.

In the satsang, on the subject of the course of birth and death, a sakhi is given from Kabirji's "Svanaid" (Maya) section. "Sva" means: the devotee's arising in this world happens differently from that of other worldly people; how the soul is contained within the egg is explained in this section. So, to understand the sakhi about the course of birth and death, it will be better understood by first looking at the sakhi that precedes it, which is —

_Na ko id upare, na ko id heth, na ko id pakhale, jiv rahe ta madhya pet ||53||_ (Svaka Id) (Kabirji says that the egg through which the soul comes is not, outside the body, in the sky; nor is it below in the netherworld; nor does this egg exist under anyone's independent authority — rather, the soul lies contained, hidden, within the belly of that egg, unseen.)

_Janma marana gati bijame, jog bhog te mahi, puran parcho vishvakun, avar na alagun chahe ||54||_ (Svaka Id ||10||) (Kabirji says the condition of a soul's birth and death lies within the seed of the egg, and within the sexual union that a soul experiences its origin is contained. The entire universe, with its eighty-four lakh species, has had the full experience of this union, and no other soul can wish to be born by any means other than this.)

On the subject of yog and bhog, in the reserved (Anamat) section, Kabirji says —

_Kabir sukh dukh sampat vipat sab, so to karma sanjog, addishta jog un mahe nahi, so to ulato amirasa bhog ||55||_ (Anamat Ang) (Kabirji says that whatever pleasure, pain, prosperity or adversity a soul obtains in this world comes about through the combination of the fruits of karma; but the unseen grace of God that a devotee receives does not fall within this fruit of karma — this soul, who is a devotee, is, contrary to the world, one who drinks the nectar-sweet essence of devotion.)

Regarding the souls of the world and His own devotees, Kabirji says —

_Kabir gyan vichar aur nij bhagat, e addishta sanjog, riddhi siddhi sampat vipat, sab e karma phal bhog ||56||_ (Anamat Ang) (Kabirji says there is an unseen, subtle bond between knowledge, reflection and the devotee — that is, through the thought of the direct realization of Parbrahm's own manifest form, this unseeable connection binds them together. Whatever riddhi, siddhi, pleasure or pain a devotee receives — all this he understands as the fruit of karma being undergone.)

Further, the satsang says —

_Kabir antariksha idu agamko, adhar rahu niradhar, nitya vikase nirman phal, trigun vriksh vistar ||40||_ (Svanaid ||3||) (Kabirji says the egg of unfathomable Nature exists in space — in the great elements — suspended without any support, and it forever develops, spreading out into the tree of the world, bringing forth the fruit that constitutes the tree of the three gunas.)

_Kabir savalakh nirmanamen, uthai nitya avaj, lakh sabad samata samai, rahata anamit gaj ||41||_ (Kudarat ||22||) (Kabirji says that in the creation of the eighty-four lakh species, within this three-gunas creation of Aum, a sound is forever arising from the one-and-a-quarter-lakh word-sounds of Aum, such as the six schools of philosophy and the rest; but out of these, a lakh of these word-sounds fall silent, while the trigunatit — beyond the three gunas — "rankar," which is held in reserve, unceasing and unbroken, goes on resounding.)

In the composition of a pada titled Bhavtaran attributed to Kabirji, in a pada headed "Shabad," it says —

Shabad:

_Cheto re cheto nar bavare, kaha achet rahai, kal daga hai sir upare, sabkun dhar khai ||1||
Lachh jiv nit khat hai, sava lakh upai hau, kahukun chhode nahi, aise kal anyai hau ||2||
Jagat chabena hai kalko, sabko khat chugai hau, chun chun khaye shurma, khate na aghai hau ||3||
Kul marjada metke, karo tum sat sagai hau, kahe Kabir tab bench hau, kal daga mit jai hau ||4||_

(Kabirji says: O foolish man, awake — why do you go about senseless? Deceitful death circles above your head; it seizes and devours everyone. Every day it eats a lakh souls and creates another lakh and a quarter, but it lets no one go — such a deceiver is it. The whole world is death's morsel, its snack; it picks everyone out one by one and devours them; it has devoured even the great heroes, one by one, and even so is never sated. So give up the bonds of family custom and ritual and join yourself truly to the true name of God — only then, Kabir says, will you be saved, and the fear of death's deceit will vanish.)

In the satsang, two sakhis of the Bij (seed) section are given, stating —

_Kabir bund athah jalhar samudra, thak mag kachhu nahi, idu trisamen bhagame, sab jag upji vilay ||43||_ (Bij ||14||) (Kabirji says the drops of water surging in the fathomless ocean are endless — their extent cannot be measured. In the same way, from just the thirtieth part of Parbrahm's egg, this world is born and merges back into dissolution; and the measure of this universe cannot be found.)

_Kabir id trisama bhagaka, bhalka chhuta ek, tine tin lok mariya, varpar nahi chhek ||44||_ (Bij ||15||) (Kabirji says that from the thirtieth part of the whole Parbrahm, only a single fragment has broken free — by it alone he has brought all three worlds under his sway. He has drawn all three worlds into a whirl, and it cannot be fathomed to its very end.)

Just as a drop of water separates out from a fathomless ocean, so from God's egg the thirtieth part has separated out; from it this entire world has been produced, and in it — the thirtieth part — that same world again dissolves, that is, is absorbed back into it. Kabirji says that the cycle of birth and death happens again and again due to the fruit of one's karma, and, on the basis of that karma-fruit, the soul also undergoes yog and bhog; the soul who has once grown fond of sense-pleasure cannot understand the other path, the path of devotion. This original source of the world's creation, Parbrahm, is unfathomable, beyond knowing; and yet the world exists coiled around him. It is forever developing, and it also perishes — that is, such coming-and-going is happening in the world at every single moment. In this universe there are thousands and lakhs of those who know and understand Parbrahm, who continuously do namasmaran (remembrance of the Name); their voices sound without ceasing, and the resonance of the many merges into Him. In the end, only one truth remains — the name of Parbrahm. Kabirji says that in the ocean there are countless, abundant drops of water, having rained down as rain; they have obtained nothing through any effort of their own — in just the same way, from the thirtieth part of Parbrahm, this entire world has come to be formed, and into it, it dissolves again. From this egg — Parbrahm — the thirtieth part that separated out (Krishna), who sustains all three worlds — this universe rests upon that support. The bond between the soul, the world, and the Lord of the world, Parbrahm, is tied by one single thread. The soul is bound to undergo the fruit of its own karma. Hence the soul, without freedom, must undergo both sin and merit. Thus, according to the law of the universe, the soul undergoes the fruit of its karma. From this karma there is no way to gain liberation except by taking refuge in the Sadguru. Because —

_Evam sansaramananni jivanyahamaddashtavan, yatha karma tatha labha iti shastranidarshanam ||13||_ (Maha Shanti 279-20) (In this way I have seen all souls caught in the cycle of birth and death. Moreover, it is also the settled view of the scriptures that as is the karma, so is the fruit obtained.)

_Kshapayitva tu tam kalam ganitam kalachodita, savasheshena kalena sambhavanti puna: puna: ||14||_ (Maha Shanti 279-18) (Having exhausted, in heaven or hell, the reckoned time of enjoying the fruit of karma, then, through the remaining karma-experience, driven onward by time together with karma, the soul is born again and again into the world.) Because —

_Kalai sampurna siddhi:_ (Samagam, Shlok 1) and _Kala: srijati bhutani_ (Samagam, Shlok 2) — in this way the entire world is subject to time. Through virtuous deeds, heaven is attained, and through sinful deeds, hell.

_Nashe'yam satatam dehi nripate punyapapayo:, tata eva samutthena tamasa rudhyate'pi cha ||15||_ (O king, the soul is not free in the matter of undergoing the fruits — pleasure and pain — of virtue and sin. It, the soul, becomes veiled by the darkness born of these very virtues and sins.)

In the Mahabharata there is a highly telling dialogue on the subject of karma between a Brahmin and a vaishya named Jajali. The vaishya Jajali explains to a Brahmin what his true karma really is. Whatever deeds are done out of desire for heaven and the like — once the soul has enjoyed their fruit and returns from there, it invites its own ruin.

_Sa eva subhago bhutva punarbhavati durbhaga:, vyapattim karmanam drishtva jugupsanti jana: sada ||16||_ (Maha Shanti 262-34) (Having enjoyed that heaven, the soul again falls under the sway of misfortune. Seeing this destruction that overtakes actions, the righteous always condemn actions done with desire.)

Because one who performs desire-driven action performs religious acts along with attachment. He who performs the Jyotishtom or Agnishtom sacrifice out of desire for heaven, or performs sacrifice to obtain a son or wealth, undergoes the fruit of that karma. Hence, if karma is not renounced before death, then even after death, though the body is no more, that karma does not perish — rather, it remains together with the soul, and the soul does not attain Parbrahm. Therefore the soul must renounce both sin and merit. Among all this, what is the essential truth? Shri Krishna tells Arjuna —

_Nirvanam paramam brahma dharmo'sau para uchyate, tasmanna chyutapurvo'hamachyutastena karmana ||17||_ (Maha Shanti 342-81) (That which is the supreme nirvana, the state of peace, Parbrahm — that alone is dharma. I have never before fallen from that state; therefore I am called Achyut, the unfallen.)

Thus, Narayan Parbrahm alone is worthy of remembrance, and it is by Him that all karma is destroyed and the supreme state may be reached.

_Harireva hi kshetragyo nirmamo nishkalastatha, jivashcha sarvabhuteshu panchabhutagunatiga: ||18||_ (348-58) (Bhagwan Shri Hari alone is the Kshetragya, the Knower of the field; he is free of possessiveness and without division; he alone, present in all beings, dwells as the soul, transcending the qualities of the five elements.) Because —

In the satsang, in Kabirji's Dedar Ang sakhi, it says —

_Kabir sab ghat bhitar sal gaman, asan adya madya anta, sikhe san jagatki, asan bhaya sab sant ||56||_ (Dedar ||42||) (Kabirji says that in every single body born into this world, Parbrahm's radiance — sal, water — moves through beginning, middle, and up to the very end; so anyone in this world who learns this hint of the mystery, the hint of God who moves in this way, and thereafter refuses to bind himself to the web of the world's maya — that is, is not willing to accept being ensnared by maya — such a person, all of them, are called sants.)

_Kabir asan bhaya ati, akala bol bandh bhav pas, chhutanko upay kahu, jo rahai ekamana vishvas ||57||_ (Dedar ||43||) (Kabirji says that sants who become extremely impatient not to be caught in the world's web of maya — even though the mind, lured by maya, may urge them toward the bond of worldly attachment — those who, in their eagerness to be free of that bondage, refuse to go toward maya, to them I show the means of release: if they keep firm-minded faith and remain untouched by maya, they will be freed from the bond of the world.)

Further, at the end of the Dedar Ang, it says —

_Kabir hun tu tehavun jab hua, tab miliya Maharaj, dilki dubadha mit gai, tab sahaj sarai sab kaj ||58||_ (Dedar ||44||) (Kabirji says when the realization came that "I and You are one," then God was met, and the mind's worries and doubts vanished; then, with natural ease, the task of attaining the vision of God's form was accomplished.)

God, who is nirgun, moves through the water of the ocean of existence from the very beginning to the very end, and pervades everywhere in the world; that God is attained by the sant who remains untouched by maya. In the satsang, finally, in Kabir's Anamat Ang sakhi, it says —

_Kabir sujh vinako sal gaman, ghat ghat raho samay, age kachhu sujhai nahi, utapat pralai jay ||45||_ (Anamat ||64||) (Kabirji says God is contained within every single body — ghat. Without the discernment and understanding by which He can be glimpsed through remaining free of sense-vices, the soul must move through the ocean of existence. Because of attachment to sense-pleasures, nothing else is visible to it, and so it must wander in the arising and dissolving of birth and death.)

One who has come to true understanding through the words of the Sadguru need not fall into the cycle of birth and death. Kabir has said —

_Ek samana sakalmen sakal samana tahi, Kabir samana bujhmen, tahan dusara nahi ||59||_ (Bijak 266) (The one Parbrahm is contained within all beings; but Kabirji says, through my true understanding, I have come to understand Ram, the indweller who shines throughout the universe, contained within the world — He is contained in that understanding, and I have come to see Parbrahm alone everywhere; no longer looking at anything else, I have become a free devotee, His servant.)

Kabirji says that Parbrahm is contained within, and dwells in, all beings. Yet, under the sway of time, one forgets that Parbrahm. Even so, in the beginning, middle, and final states, if the soul, becoming free of karma, can recognize Parbrahm, it can go to Parbrahm's abode; but if it goes on following the ways of the world, then the cycle of birth and death continues without end; yet if it has kept the company of sants, it can cross over the ocean of existence.

Parbrahm dwells in every single body, but without the company of the Sadguru, the discernment does not come, and so no path ahead is visible, and the soul remains stuck in this ocean of existence.

For this, they have called Kabirji the Lord of the world and the universe. That is to say, those beings who are under the sway of maya — their worship, and their notion of God, regarding the deity they follow as God, is a separate matter from the worship of the sants and Parbrahm's own devotees, whose devotion is unattached and free of the world. Jivanji Maharaj says that those whose god is Shiva, Brahma, and the like — even they exist within the eighty-four lakh species; so those who remain within these eighty-four lakh species and follow deity-worship, vows and the like — even though Parbrahm pervades and dwells within every single body, they are unable to touch Him. In the end, their servants and worshippers do not attain liberation from the eighty-four lakh species, and they must wander here and there in the world. But whoever seeks out the true Sadguru and takes refuge with him need have no worry at all, because he becomes free of desire and devotes himself wholly to devotion. So he no longer has any other fear, because —

_Maranako dar Hari nam bin, dise sab sansar, harijan ugare jivana, so Sadguruke upkar ||60||_ (In the world, whoever is without the name of Parbrahm lives in fear of death. But by the Sadguru's grace, the Harijan crosses this ocean of existence with the support of the "Name" — he alone is truly fearless.) Because —

_Nirbhay khat Kabirki, sab santan lini bant, take kachhu nahi jivana, jake man men ant ||61||_ (All of us have Kabirji as our Sadguru, and his presence is fearless. So all sants and devotees have accepted Kabirji's name. But for those whose minds are still caught up in the world's maya, and in whose minds there is still confusion and doubt — for such souls, Jivanji Maharaj says he has nothing more to say, because they are bound to drown and perish in the ocean of existence.)

In the satsang, in the chapter on Mayabrahma's Bhel, the first two lines quoted are from a pada by Kabirji. The next two lines of this same pada, "Panch tatva trigun shakat kari saniya," are given at the end of this chapter, "Vachan Ej Parmeshwar" —

_Akarki ot akar nahi ubare, Shiv Virinchi Vishnu ja tanhi, jasaka sevak tas, bhal bhavahi, ishtakun chhod age na jai ||46||_ (Kabirji says: if one form remains sheltered under the cover of another form, then when that sheltering form perishes, the form dependent on it cannot survive either. In this matter, even great gods like Shiva, Brahma, or Vishnu — when, at the dissolution of this creation, these three great gods themselves also perish, then the devotees who took refuge in those gods also perish along with them. So whoever is a devoted servant, worshipping and adoring some deity, merges into that deity's own refuge, and cannot go forward, leaving his chosen deity behind, to take shelter with one who stands even higher than that deity.)

Namdev has written a pada about the fate that befalls whoever worships whatever deity —

_Na taris na taris Ram bina,
jap le ho jivda tu Ram nam ||teka||
jaldev pujila to kachla hoyla,
bhagati na hoyla Ram bina ||1||
Chandi pujila to mrigla hoyla,
bhagati na hoyla Ram bina ||2||
Devi pujila to bhensa hoyla,
bhagati na hoyla Ram bina ||3||
Harsadi pujila to rudhir piyela,
bhagati na hoyla Ram bina ||4||
Khetrapal pujila to kukra hoyla,
bhagati na hoyla Ram bina ||5||
Ganesa pujila to musa hoyla,
bhagati na hoyla Ram bina ||6||
Mahadev pujila to vrishabh hoyla,
bhagati na hoyla Ram bina ||7||
Suraj pujila to ashva hoyla,
bhagati na hoyla Ram bina ||8||
Sannyasi pujila to Shivlok jayla,
bhagati na hoyla Ram bina ||9||
Brahman pujila to sargalok jayla,
bhagati na hoyla Ram bina ||10||
Bhagat pujila to bhagta hoyla,
janam janam Namdev nishan bajayla ||1||_

(Namdevji says: O soul, you will not cross over without Ram, so chant the name of Ram. If you worship the water-god, you will become a wave, a crab — devotion will not come about without Ram. If you worship Chandi, you will become a deer, an animal; worship Devi, you will become a buffalo; worship Harshad Mata, you will have to drink blood — note: when the messengers of Yama lead a sinful soul to hell, and that thirsty soul, tormented by the sun's heat, begs for water, Harshad Mata, seated at a water-stall along the way, gives exactly as much water as the amount of blood she receives; since this Harshad Mata is blood-thirsty, she can only give her worshipper blood in return. Worship Kshetrapal, you will have to become a dog. Worship Ganpati, you will have to become a mouse. Worship Mahadev, you will have to become a bull, an ox. Worship Surya, you will have to become a horse. Serve a sannyasi, you will go to Shivlok; worship Brahma, you will go to Swarglok. But if you worship a devotee (bhagat), you too will become a devotee, and you will remain a devotee birth after birth — this proclamation Namdev has sounded and spread abroad.)

Vyasji too has composed a pada of this same sentiment (Raag Ramkali) —

_Jaki upasana tahiki vasana, tahiko namrup gun gaiyai,
yahai ananya dharma paripati, Vrindavan basi anat na jaiyai ||teka||
soi bibhachari an kahai an karai takau mukh dekhen darun dukh paiyai,
Vyas hoi upahas tras kiyai, as achhat kit das kahaiyai ||2||_

(Vyasji says: whatever deity one worships, one carries within oneself a longing for that deity, and one ought to sing the name, form and praises of that same deity — this is the way of exclusive devotion, fixed on one alone: so that one who dwells in Vrindavan ought not to go anywhere else. But if such a person says one thing and does another, then he is to be counted an adulterer in devotion; even to look upon his face brings terrible suffering. So Vyasji says: if, while posing as the worshipper of one's chosen deity, a person disregards and mocks that deity, tyrannizing it, then even the slight hope he might have of being called that deity's devotee is itself found wanting — so how then could he be called that deity's devotee?)

In the Bijak, Kabir has spoken this sakhi —

_Bhakti bhakti sabkoi kahai, bhakti na ai kaj, jahanko kiya bharosava, tahante ai gaj ||62||_ (Everyone goes about saying "devotion, devotion," and performs devotion to various deities, but that devotion proved useless in the end — whatever deity one placed one's trust in gave assurance for a while, and all of them were of the nature of time; time carried its worshippers off into its own realm — but when the great dissolution came, both the chosen deity and its worshipper perished, and when the world was created anew, both were born again according to their karma.)

(Explaining "Akarki Ot," revered Yadunath Maharaj writes: "behind a form that has hands and feet, another form cannot survive.") In the Gita, chapter 7, verses 22-23, it says —

_Sa tatha shraddhaya yuktastasyaradhanamihate, labhate cha tata: kamanmayaiva vihitanhi tan ||19||
Antavattu phalam teshan tadbhavatyalpamedhasam,
devandevayajo yanti madbhakta yanti mamapi ||20||_

Meaning: He, endowed with that faith, worships that deity, and through that deity he obtains the desired enjoyments that I Myself have ordained. ||22||
